title: Etiquette & language
body:
Onsen etiquette matters directly on this trip — Ginzan Onsen's whole draw is the bath. Wash and rinse fully at the taps before entering the shared water; no soap or shampoo in the bath itself; swimsuits aren't worn in a traditional onsen.

Visible tattoos aren't illegal in Japan, but many traditional ryokan still restrict them as facility policy rather than law. If anyone in the group has visible tattoos, ask the ryokan about a private/family bath (kashikiri-buro) reservation when booking — this wasn't individually confirmed for Ginzan Onsen's specific properties this pass.

Shoes come off at the genkan (entryway) of any ryokan, and at Risshaku-ji's temple buildings. Keep voices down in shared bath areas.
